title: What Depp v. Heard Means for #MeToo

sentences.en: Hey, I'm Benjamin Poulin and I'm Mark Ronson and welcome to The Reframers, a podcast that's all about the love of design and the culture that surrounds it.
sentences.zh: 嘿，我是本杰明·普兰，我是马克·罗森，欢迎收听《重构者》，这是一档专注于设计之美及其周围文化的播客。

sentences.en: Even back when I was DJing in nightclubs in the era of vinyl,
sentences.zh: 甚至在我还在黑胶唱片时代的女王夜店里打碟的时候，

sentences.en: every night you took 300 of your most prized possessions to work with you and you turned a DJ booth into this like living pop-up museum of beautiful 50-year-old artifacts.
sentences.zh: 每天晚上你都要带着300件你最珍爱的传家宝去工作，你把DJ台变成了一个充满美丽50年历史文物的活体快闪博物馆。

sentences.en: Listen to The Reframers from Audemars Piguet now on your favorite podcast platforMs.
sentences.zh: 现在就在你喜爱的播客平台上收听来自爱彼的《重构者》。

sentences.en: From New York Times, I'm Michael Barbaro.
sentences.zh: 来自《纽约时报》，我是迈克尔·巴尔巴罗。

sentences.en: This is Daily.
sentences.zh: 这是《每日新闻》。

sentences.en: Last week, when a jury sided with Johnny Depp over Amber Heard, it validated a legal strategy in which the accused turned the tables on their accusers.
sentences.zh: 上周，当陪审团裁定约翰尼·德普胜诉、安珀·赫德败诉时，它证实了一种法律策略，即被告将矛头对准原告反戈一击。

sentences.en: Today, my colleague, Julia Jacobs, on how that strategy could fundamentally change the dynamics of the Me Too era.
sentences.zh: 今天，我的同事茱莉亚·雅各布斯将探讨这种策略如何从根本上改变“我也是”时代的动态。

sentences.en: This is Monday, June 6th.
sentences.zh: 今天是6月6日，星期一。

sentences.en: Julia, since the verdict in the trial of Johnny Depp and Amber Heard came down last week, there has been an impassioned debate about what exactly it means.
sentences.zh: 茱莉亚，自从上周约翰尼·德普和安珀·赫德的诉讼案宣判以来，关于它到底意味着什么，引发了热烈的争论。

sentences.en: And we called several of our colleagues in the newsroom after the verdict came out and asked them, what does it mean?
sentences.zh: 我们在宣判后给新闻室的几位同事打了电话，问他们：这到底意味着什么？

sentences.en: And you had a very clear-eyed answer.
sentences.zh: 而你给出了一个非常清醒的答案。

sentences.en: And so that's what we want to discuss with you, what you think this case and its outcome means.
sentences.zh: 所以这就是我们想要和你讨论的，你认为这个案件及其结果意味着什么。

sentences.en: Well, Michael, it's important to note that this is a case with a unique set of facts and a very complicated set of facts.
sentences.zh: 嗯，迈克尔，需要指出的是，这是一个具有独特事实以及非常复杂事实的案件。

sentences.en: But what I've been told by legal experts in the wake of the verdict is that this is an important moment for a legal strategy that has emerged since the birth of the Me Too movement.
sentences.zh: 但法律专家在判决后告诉我，对于自“我也是”运动诞生以来出现的一种法律策略而言，这是一个关键时刻。

sentences.en: Since women started coming forward and accusing men of abuse and harassment, the accused have adopted a strategy of suing their alleged victims for defaming them.
sentences.zh: 自从女性开始站出来指控男性虐待和骚扰以来，被指控者采取了一种反诉策略，起诉所谓的受害者诽谤他们。

sentences.en: Essentially accusing them of lying.
sentences.zh: 本质上是控告他们在说谎。

sentences.en: And what, Julia, is the goal of that strategy?
sentences.zh: 茱莉亚，这种策略的目的是什么？

sentences.en: For people who've been accused of wrongdoing, the goal is to get a form of justice, a sense of redemption for themselves.
sentences.zh: 对于被指控有不当行为的人来说，其目的是为了获得某种正义感，为自己正名。

sentences.en: It's about clearing their name and trying to establish what the truth was of this relationship or this incident in a public court of law.
sentences.zh: 这是为了洗清他们的罪名，并试图在公开法庭上确定这段关系或这起事件的真相。

sentences.en: And so these accused perpetrators are trying to flip the script in a way and say that they are the victims of defamation.
sentences.zh: 因此，这些被指控的施害者正试图换一种说法，宣称自己才是诽谤的受害者。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: And this is the kind of lawsuit, a defamation lawsuit, that was filed by Johnny Depp against his ex-wife, Amber Heard.
sentences.zh: 这就是约翰尼·德普对他的前妻安珀·赫德提起的那种诉讼，即诽谤诉讼。

sentences.en: Just remind us about those circumstances.
sentences.zh: 请提醒我们注意这些情况。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: So Depp sued his ex-wife, Amber Heard, for defamation.
sentences.zh: 因此，德普起诉他的前妻安珀·赫德诽谤。

sentences.en: And this was over an op-ed that The Washington Post published in 2018.
sentences.zh: 这是针对《华盛顿邮报》2018年发表的一篇专栏文章。

sentences.en: This was not long after the fall of Harvey Weinstein.
sentences.zh: 这发生在哈维·韦恩斯坦倒台后不久。

sentences.en: And the op-ed basically says that her life was harmed after she went public with domestic abuse allegations.
sentences.zh: 这篇专栏文章基本上说，在她公开家庭虐待指控后，她的生活受到了损害。

sentences.en: And to be clear, she does not mention Johnny Depp's name once.
sentences.zh: 需要明确的是，她一次也没有提到约翰尼·德普的名字。

sentences.en: But she does write that two years ago, she becomes a public figure representing domestic abuse.
sentences.zh: 但她确实写道，两年前，她成为了代表家庭虐待的公众人物。

sentences.en: Those words are very critical in this case.
sentences.zh: 这些话在这个案件中至关重要。

sentences.en: Got it.
sentences.zh: 明白了。

sentences.en: And she said that she felt the full force of our culture's wrath for women who speak out.
sentences.zh: 她说，她感受到了我们文化对发声女性的全方位怒火。

sentences.en: And so even though she doesn't say his name, it's clear she's referring to a time in 2016 when she accused him of abuse.
sentences.zh: 因此，尽管她没有说出他的名字，但很明显她指的是2016年她指控他虐待的那段时期。

sentences.en: And Depp feels like this op-ed is clearly referring to him and everyone knows it.
sentences.zh: 德普觉得这篇专栏文章显然是在指他，而且人尽皆知。

sentences.en: Mm-hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯哼。

sentences.en: And the result of everyone knowing it is that he's losing work, he's losing his status as this world-famous actor.
sentences.zh: 人尽皆知的结果是，他失去了工作，失去了这位世界知名演员的地位。

sentences.en: Mm-hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯哼。

sentences.en: So as a result, a few months after the op-ed is published, he sues.
sentences.zh: 因此，在这篇专栏文章发表几个月后，他提起了诉讼。

sentences.en: So after he files this defamation lawsuit and it gets closer and closer to trial, legal experts are telling me this is going to be an uphill battle for him to win.
sentences.zh: 所以在他提起这起诽谤诉讼并且离审判越来越近时，法律专家告诉我，对他来说这将是一场硬仗。

sentences.en: Why?
sentences.zh: 为什么？

sentences.en: Well, he lost a similar case in Britain and he also sued for defamation there, but he didn't sue Amber Heard.
sentences.zh: 嗯，他在英国输掉了一起类似案件，他在那里也起诉了诽谤，但他没有起诉安珀·赫德。

sentences.en: He sued the publisher of a British tabloid, The Sun.
sentences.zh: 他起诉了一家英国小报《太阳报》的出版商。

sentences.en: And The Sun called him a wife-beater in a headline.
sentences.zh: 《太阳报》在一篇头条新闻中称他是打老婆的人。

sentences.en: Mm-hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯哼。

sentences.en: And so I read the decision in that case.
sentences.zh: 所以我读了该案的判决书。

sentences.en: It was 120-something pages.
sentences.zh: 有120多页。

sentences.en: And the judge determined that what The Sun published was substantially true based on evidence that he said made him believe that most of Heard's accounts of abuse were true.
sentences.zh: 法官根据他所说的话认定《太阳报》发表的内容基本属实，这些证据让他相信赫德关于虐待的大部分陈述都是真的。

sentences.en: So another reason it's an uphill battle is because defamation cases are easier to win in the U.K.
sentences.zh: 他面临艰难之战的另一个原因是，在英国诽谤案更容易打赢，

sentences.en: and Depp lost in this case.
sentences.zh: 而德普在这个案件中输了。

sentences.en: Mm-hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯哼。

sentences.en: So legal experts expected that his chances would be even worse in the United States.
sentences.zh: 因此，法律专家预计他在美国的胜算会更低。

sentences.en: And Julia, what is the legal bar for proving defamation in the United States?
sentences.zh: 茱莉亚，在美国证明诽谤的法律标准是什么？

sentences.en: So in the United States, the burden of proof is on the plaintiff, in this case Johnny Depp,
sentences.zh: 在美国，举证责任在原告一方，本案中即约翰尼·德普，

sentences.en: to prove that what was said about them was untrue and the statement was made with actual malice.
sentences.zh: 他需要证明关于他们的言论是不真实的，且该陈述是在极度恶意的情况下做出的。

sentences.en: Which means basically that the person knew they were lying, knew what they were saying was false, or they had a high degree of awareness that the statement was probably false.
sentences.zh: 这基本上意味着此人知道自己在说谎，知道他们所说的是虚假的，或者他们高度意识到该陈述可能是虚假的。

sentences.en: Hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯。

sentences.en: So a relatively high bar to prove that someone making an accusation like this knows that it's false, which seems like a difficult thing to establish,
sentences.zh: 因此，要证明一个提出这种指控的人知道这是虚假的，标准相对较高，这似乎是一件很难确立的事情，

sentences.en: and therefore did it nevertheless with malice to try to hurt the person they were accusing.
sentences.zh: 因此他们仍然出于恶意去这样做，试图伤害他们指控的人。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: Well, as we know, Depp was able to meet that legal bar.
sentences.zh: 如我们所知，德普达到了这一法律标准。

sentences.en: The jury, in this case, found that Amber Heard had defamed him and owed him millions of dollars as a result.
sentences.zh: 本案陪审团裁定安珀·赫德诽谤了他，因此判决她赔偿数百万美元。

sentences.en: So let's go through the trial to understand how a jury might have come to the result.
sentences.zh: 让我们回顾一下庭审过程，以了解陪审团是如何得出这一结果的。

sentences.en: It did, especially given what you and the lawyers you talked to have just described as, you know, the relatively high bar for accomplishing this.
sentences.zh: 确实如此，尤其是考虑到你和你交谈过的律师刚才所描述的，你知道，达成这一目标的相对较高的标准。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: So to be clear, I was watching from the comfort of my office and my home, like many were, over live stream.
sentences.zh: 需要说明的是，我和许多人一样，是通过直播在舒适的办公室和家里观看的。

sentences.en: And that was because the public fervor over this trial was so intense.
sentences.zh: 这是因为公众对这场审判的热情实在太高了。

sentences.en: People were lining up in the middle of the night just to get seats.
sentences.zh: 人们半夜排队只为了买到座位。

sentences.en: And honestly, my focus was on what was being said in the courtroom.
sentences.zh: 老实说，我的注意力集中在法庭上说了什么。

sentences.en: So I decided to watch the live stream.
sentences.zh: 所以我决定看直播。

sentences.en: All right.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: Good morning.
sentences.zh: 早上好。

sentences.en: Good morning.
sentences.zh: 早上好。

sentences.en: All right.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: Do we have any...
sentences.zh: 我们有什么……

sentences.en: At the beginning of the trial, we're in April.
sentences.zh: 在审判开始时，时间是四月。

sentences.en: Good morning.
sentences.zh: 早上好。

sentences.en: For nearly 30 years, Mr. Depp built a reputation as one of the most talented actors in Hollywood.
sentences.zh: 近30年来，德普先生树立了自己作为好莱坞最有才华演员之一的声誉。

sentences.en: Depp's lawyers start opening arguments.
sentences.zh: 德普的律师开始发表开案陈词。

sentences.en: A respected artist whose name was associated with success at the box office.
sentences.zh: 一位受人尊敬的艺术家，其名字与票房成功联系在一起。

sentences.en: Today, his name is associated with a lie, a false statement uttered by his former wife, the defendant, Amber Heard.
sentences.zh: 今天，他的名字与一个谎言联系在一起，这是他的前妻、被告安珀·赫德说出的虚假陈述。

sentences.en: And it's very clear from the beginning that they're making this argument that Amber Heard is an all out liar.
sentences.zh: 从一开始就很明显，他们提出了安珀·赫德是个彻头彻尾的骗子的论点。

sentences.en: No one had ever, in five decades, no one had ever accused Johnny Depp of being abusive of any kind with a woman.
sentences.zh: 在过去的五十年里，没有人，从来没有人指控约翰尼·德普对女性有任何形式的虐待。

sentences.en: That she's lying about every accusation of domestic abuse.
sentences.zh: 她对家庭虐待的每一项指控都在撒谎。

sentences.en: By choosing to lie about her husband for her own personal benefit, Amber Heard forever changed Mr. Depp's life and reputation.
sentences.zh: 通过选择为自己的个人利益而污蔑她的丈夫，安珀·赫德永远改变了德普先生的生活和声誉。

sentences.en: And that she's doing it, you know, as they wrote in their lawsuit, because she wants to become a, quote, darling of the Me Too movement.
sentences.zh: 正如他们在诉讼中所写的那样，她这样做是因为她想成为所谓的“我也是”运动的宠儿。

sentences.en: All right.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: Opening statements.
sentences.zh: 开案陈词。

sentences.en: Yes, ma'am.
sentences.zh: 是的，女士。

sentences.en: Mr. Rottenborn.
sentences.zh: 罗滕博恩先生。

sentences.en: On the other side of the courtroom, we have Heard and her legal team making their argument.
sentences.zh: 在法庭的另一边，赫德和她的法律团队提出了他们的论点。

sentences.en: What this case is about is about the First Amendment, about that December 18th, 2018 op-ed piece,
sentences.zh: 这个案件关乎第一修正案，关乎2018年12月18日的那篇专栏文章，

sentences.en: and whether Ms. Heard's freedom of speech and the First Amendment give her the right to say the words that she said.
sentences.zh: 以及赫德女士的言论自由和第一修正案是否赋予了她发表这些言论的权利。

sentences.en: That right, that freedom of speech, is what Amber Heard is asking you to uphold and protect in this lawsuit.
sentences.zh: 这种权利，这种言论自由，正是安珀·赫德在这起诉讼中请求你们维护和保护的。

sentences.en: They say that what Heard wrote in the op-ed is protected by the First Amendment.
sentences.zh: 他们表示，赫德在专栏文章中所写的内容受第一修正案保护。

sentences.en: The evidence will show that Amber did suffer domestic abuse at the hands of Johnny Depp.
sentences.zh: 证据将表明，安珀确实遭受了约翰尼·德普带来的家庭虐待。

sentences.en: And it took many forMs.
sentences.zh: 它有许多形式。

sentences.en: Physical, sure.
sentences.zh: 当然有身体上的。

sentences.en: But also emotional, verbal, psychological abuse.
sentences.zh: 但还有情感、言语、心理上的虐待。

sentences.en: It's all domestic abuse that she suffered at his hands.
sentences.zh: 这都是她在他的手下遭受的家庭虐待。

sentences.en: And that every word of her account of abuse is true.
sentences.zh: 她对虐待经历的每一句话都是真的。

sentences.en: You'll hear evidence of crushing drug and alcohol abuse.
sentences.zh: 你们会听到毁灭性药物和酒精滥用的证据。

sentences.en: You'll hear evidence of Depp taking more drugs than you can count.
sentences.zh: 你们会听到德普吸毒过量的证据。

sentences.en: And that all the damages to Depp's career are his fault and a result of his substance abuse probleMs.
sentences.zh: 德普事业遭受的所有损害都是他自己的错，是他滥用药物问题造成的后果。

sentences.en: You'll hear evidence that the same addictions that led him to abuse Amber also led to the demise of his career as an actor.
sentences.zh: 你们会听到这样的证据：导致他虐待安珀的同一种瘾癖也导致了他演员生涯的终结。

sentences.en: Not Heard's fault.
sentences.zh: 这不是赫德的错。

sentences.en: So any damages that he suffered in his career are not because of this op-ed.
sentences.zh: 因此他在职业生涯中遭受的任何损失都不是因为这篇专栏文章。

sentences.en: And it's time to make Johnny take responsibility.
sentences.zh: 是时候让约翰尼承担责任了。

sentences.en: To tell him, Mr. Depp, stop blaming other people for your self-created probleMs.
sentences.zh: 告诉他，德普先生，不要再把你自己创造的问题怪罪到别人头上。

sentences.en: To take responsibility for your own life.
sentences.zh: 为自己的生活承担责任。

sentences.en: And it's up to you, ladies and gentlemen, to make him do that.
sentences.zh: 女士们先生们，这就要靠你们来让他这样做了。

sentences.en: And so their argument to the jury is, look, this is a very easy case.
sentences.zh: 因此，他们向陪审团提出的论点是，听着，这是一个非常简单的案件。

sentences.en: Look at this single piece of paper at the center of this case, this op-ed.
sentences.zh: 看看这个案件中心的单张纸，这篇专栏文章。

sentences.en: Are these statements true?
sentences.zh: 这些陈述是真的吗？

sentences.en: And their answer is yes.
sentences.zh: 他们的回答是肯定的。

sentences.en: Mm-hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯哼。

sentences.en: So given all of that, and with the benefit now of hindsight, what end up being the key moments in this trial?
sentences.zh: 鉴于这一切，现在事后回想起来，这场审判的关键时刻究竟是什么？

sentences.en: So the center of this trial was a testimony of Johnny Depp and Amber Heard.
sentences.zh: 所以这场审判的核心是约翰尼·德普和安珀·赫德的证词。

sentences.en: They both testified over four days.
sentences.zh: 他们两人的作证都持续了四天。

sentences.en: And when they were on that stand being questioned by their own lawyers, they were giving very specific narratives of what their relationship with the other person looked like.
sentences.zh: 当他们站在证人席上接受各自律师的盘问时，他们对彼此的关系给出了非常具体的描述。

sentences.en: Mm-hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯哼。

sentences.en: But when they were cross-examined by the other side's lawyers, they were challenged on those accounts.
sentences.zh: 但当他们接受对方律师的交叉盘问时，这些说法受到了性质上的质疑。

sentences.en: They were challenged on the accounts of who they were in the relationship and what occurred during the relationship.
sentences.zh: 他们在关系中的角色以及关系期间发生的事情的说法受到了挑战。

sentences.en: All right.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: You can have a seat.
sentences.zh: 请坐。

sentences.en: All right.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: Cross-examination.
sentences.zh: 交叉盘问。

sentences.en: Thank you, Your Honor.
sentences.zh: 谢谢法官阁下。

sentences.en: Under cross-examination, Heard's lawyers confronted him with text messages and emails that they say go to show that he's the abuser.
sentences.zh: 在交叉盘问中，赫德的律师用短信和电子邮件质问他，他们认为这些证据表明他才是虐待者。

sentences.en: And one of the most graphic examples of that is a text message from 2013.
sentences.zh: 其中最生动的例子之一是2013年的一条短信。

sentences.en: This is at the beginning of their relationship.
sentences.zh: 这是在他们关系的初期。

sentences.en: And in this text, Mr. Depp.
sentences.zh: 在这条短信中，德普先生。

sentences.en: Depp writes to a friend, the actor, Paul Bettany, actually.
sentences.zh: 德普给一个朋友写信，也就是演员保罗·贝坦尼。

sentences.en: You text Mr. Bettany, let's burn Amber.

sentences.en: So, Julia, what does this verdict mean for the accused and the accusers?
sentences.zh: 那么，朱莉娅，这个裁决对被告和原告意味着什么？

sentences.en: And let's start with the accused, because at the start of our conversation,
sentences.zh: 让我们先从被告说起，因为在我们对话刚开始时，

sentences.en: you said that defamation lawsuits like the one Johnny Depp brought against Amber Heard are an increasingly popular approach for people accused of sexual abuse or assault.
sentences.zh: 你提到，像约翰尼·德普对安德鲁·赫德提起的那种诽谤诉讼，正成为被指控性虐待或性侵犯的人越来越受欢迎的一种手段。

sentences.en: So, the morning after the verdict, I talked to a lawyer.
sentences.zh: 因此，在宣判后的第二天早上，我采访了一位律师。

sentences.en: His name is Andrew Miltenberg, and he regularly represents people who are accused of sexual misconduct.
sentences.zh: 他叫安德鲁·米尔滕伯格，经常代表被指控性行为不端的人。

sentences.en: And he represents these people in defamation cases against their accusers.
sentences.zh: 他在针对原告的诽谤案件中代表这些人。

sentences.en: He said he got about a dozen emails from clients after the verdict expressing that they thought this def verdict would bode well for them,
sentences.zh: 他说，宣判后他收到了客户大约十几封电子邮件，表示他们认为这个诽谤裁决对他们是个好兆头，

sentences.en: that it could send a positive signal for their cases.
sentences.zh: 这可能为他们的案件发出积极的信号。

sentences.en: And as their lawyer, he obviously has to caution them that every case is different, that they're not Johnny Depp,
sentences.zh: 作为他们的律师，他显然必须提醒他们，每个案件都是不同的，他们不是约翰尼·德普，

sentences.en: they're not a massive movie star with a fan base live tweeting in support of them and defending their every word online.
sentences.zh: 他们不是那种拥有庞大粉丝群、在网上直播发推支持并为其每一句话辩护的超级电影明星。

sentences.en: And there's no legal precedent set in this Virginia case that, say, a jury in New York would have to follow.
sentences.zh: 而且在这个弗吉尼亚州的案件中，并没有设立诸如纽约陪审团必须遵循的法律先例。

sentences.en: But this lawyer did acknowledge that the verdict sends a positive signal to an accused plaintiff like his clients,
sentences.zh: 但这位律师确实承认，该裁决向像他的客户这样的被告原告发出了一个积极的信号，

sentences.en: a signal that a jury in a case like this could be willing to side with the accused, who has sued the accuser for defamation.
sentences.zh: 即类似案件中的陪审团可能愿意站在起诉原告诽谤的被告一边。

sentences.en: And the message is that this powerful legal tool that has always, in theory, been available to people accused of sexual misconduct, a defamation lawsuit,
sentences.zh: 传递出的信息是，这个理论上一直可供被指控性行为不端的人使用的强大法律武器——诽谤诉讼，

sentences.en: but was seen as difficult to pull off, now looks a lot more attractive.
sentences.zh: 虽然以前被认为很难成功，现在看起来却吸引力大增。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And most of the lawsuits are settled or dismissed by a judge.
sentences.zh: 而且大多数诉讼都是庭外和解或被法官驳回的。

sentences.en: This is a rare defamation lawsuit that actually makes it to trial.
sentences.zh: 这是一起罕见的、真正走到审判阶段的诽谤诉讼。

sentences.en: And the reason that so many settle is because few people in the world want embarrassing, intimate details out on display in front of the public during legal proceedings.
sentences.zh: 之所以有那么多案件选择和解，是因为世界上很少有人愿意在法律诉讼期间将尴尬的私密细节公之于众。

sentences.en: So, you know, why not settle outside of court?
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道，为什么不选择庭外和解呢？

sentences.en: But this lawyer, Andrew Miltenberg,
sentences.zh: 但这位律师安德鲁·米尔滕伯格

sentences.en: said he can see a world in which plaintiffs feel emboldened to bring these cases into the public to try to find the redemption that Johnny Depp seems to have achieved,
sentences.zh: 表示，他可以看到这样一种情况：原告们会感到受到鼓舞，将这些案件闹上法庭，试图寻找约翰尼·德普似乎已经取得的救赎，

sentences.en: at least so far.
sentences.zh: 至少目前是这样。

sentences.en: So, in theory, this could mean a lot more defamation lawsuits and defamation trials could be coming.
sentences.zh: 因此，从理论上讲，这意味着未来可能会有更多的诽谤诉讼和诽谤审判。

sentences.en: It's possible.
sentences.zh: 这是有可能的。

sentences.en: And there are already cases like these working their way through the court system.
sentences.zh: 而且已经有一些类似案件正在法院系统中审理。

sentences.en: One of the most prominent ones is actually a lawsuit filed by Marilyn Manson, the musician,
sentences.zh: 其中最引人注目的一起是由音乐家玛丽莲·曼森提起的诉讼，

sentences.en: who happens to be a good friend of Depp and was brought up frequently throughout the trial.
sentences.zh: 他恰好是德普的好友，在整个审判过程中也多次被提及。

sentences.en: And Manson sued his accuser, who said that he sexually assaulted her.
sentences.zh: 曼森起诉了指控他性侵的指控者。

sentences.en: And another major case we have coming, this is someone that this lawyer, Miltenberg, represents, is filed by the writer Stephen Elliott,
sentences.zh: 我们迎来的另一个重大案件是由作家斯蒂芬·埃利奥特发起的，他是律师米尔滕伯格的客户之一，

sentences.en: who was included in a crowdsourced list of men in media who had misbehaved somehow.
sentences.zh: 他曾被列入一份由众包整理的、涉及某种不当行为的媒体男性名单中。

sentences.en: In his case, he was accused of sexual assault, which he has denied.
sentences.zh: 在他的案子中，他被指控性侵，但他对此予以否认。

sentences.en: And he sued the creator of that list for defamation.
sentences.zh: 他起诉了该名单的创建者诽谤。

sentences.zh: 所以，我们一直在讨论这个裁决对被告意味着什么。

sentences.en: Primarily, these men who, from what you have found, are more emboldened to pursue a strategy of suing their accusers for defamation.
sentences.zh: 主要是这些男性，根据你的调查，他们更加大胆地采取起诉原告诽谤的策略。

sentences.en: But what does this verdict mean for those who have made the accusations of sexual assault or sexual abuse?
sentences.zh: 但这个裁决对于那些提出性侵犯或性虐待指控的人意味着什么呢？

sentences.en: So, I talk to lawyers who consult with accusers who are considering coming forward with their accounts of abuse, even potentially through op-eds like Amber Heard did.
sentences.zh: 因此，我采访了一些律师，他们为考虑公开指控虐待经历的原告提供咨询，甚至可能像安德鲁·赫德那样通过专栏文章的形式。

sentences.en: And the fear that I'm hearing from them is that they'll see how Depp v.
sentences.zh: 我从他们那里听到的恐惧是，他们会看到“德普诉赫德案”的结局，然后心里会想，为什么我要站出来提出一个可能导致自己被起诉的主张，

sentences.en: Heard played out, and they'll think to themselves, why should I come forward with a claim that could possibly result in me being sued,
sentences.zh: 花上几年时间去为一场诉讼辩护，并在诉讼费上花一大笔钱？

sentences.en: spending years defending a lawsuit in which I spend a whole lot of money on legal fees?
sentences.zh: 然后，到头来，我可能会输，还必须向我指控行为不端的人支付一大笔钱。

sentences.en: And then, in the end, I might lose and have to pay the person I accused of misconduct a lot of money.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Right.

sentences.en: And so, this fear is particularly heightened around this case, I think, because you have a situation where they saw this as a case that was very unlikely for Johnny Depp to win.
sentences.zh: 出于我们讨论过的原因，就美国的诽谤法而言，

sentences.en: For the reasons we discussed, in terms of defamation law in the United States,
sentences.zh: 还因为在这个案子中，有一位夫妻治疗师作证说这段关系中存在相互虐待。

sentences.en: but also because we had a case where a couples therapist testified that there was mutual abuse in this relationship.
sentences.zh: 最终，这些律师认为，陪审团绝不可能一致裁定这篇专栏文章中涉案的陈述构成诽谤。

sentences.en: And, ultimately, these lawyers thought that there was no way a jury could find unanimously that the statements at issue in this op-ed were defamatory.

sentences.en: But they did.
sentences.zh: 我们必须记住，“我也是”运动最初的目的之一，是为女性创造一个空间，让她们能够站出来，而不必担心自己的生活会被那些比她们更有权势、更有资源的男性所摧毁。
